# Resource: stripe_climate_order

A purchase of carbon removal from Stripe Climate. Set exactly one of `metric_tons` (a whole number of tons) and `amount` (the money to spend, in the smallest unit of the order's currency). The order spends the account's available balance in its settlement currency. `terraform destroy` cancels the order and refunds its `amount_subtotal`, but not its `amount_fees`; Stripe cannot delete an order, so a canceled order stays in the account. Stripe cancels only orders that are not yet delivered, so destroy leaves a delivered order as it is, with a warning. Only `beneficiary` and `metadata` change in place: changing any other argument cancels the order and buys a new one, and the fees of the canceled order are not refunded.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_climate_product" "removal" {
  id = "climsku_123"
}

# Spends your available balance. Destroying the order cancels it and refunds the removal,
# but not Stripe's fees.
resource "stripe_climate_order" "offset" {
  product     = data.stripe_climate_product.removal.id
  metric_tons = "1"

  beneficiary = {
    public_name = "Acme Inc."
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `product` - (Required) Unique identifier of the Climate product. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `amount` - (Optional) Requested amount of carbon removal units. Either this or `metric_tons` must be specified. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `beneficiary` - (Optional) Publicly sharable reference for the end beneficiary of carbon removal. Assumed to be the Stripe account if not set. See [`beneficiary`](#beneficiary) below.
* `currency` - (Optional) Request currency for the order as a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a supported [settlement currency for your account](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). If omitted, the account's default currency will be used. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `metric_tons` - (Optional) Requested number of tons for the order. Either this or `amount` must be specified. Changing it replaces the resource.

<a id="beneficiary"></a>
### `beneficiary`

The `beneficiary` attribute supports:

* `public_name` - (Required) Publicly displayable name for the end beneficiary of carbon removal.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `amount_fees` - Total amount of [Frontier](https://frontierclimate.com/)'s service fees in the currency's smallest unit.
* `amount_subtotal` - Total amount of the carbon removal in the currency's smallest unit.
* `amount_total` - Total amount of the order including fees in the currency's smallest unit.
* `canceled_at` - Time at which the order was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `cancellation_reason` - Reason for the cancellation of this order. Possible values: `expired`, `product_unavailable`, `requested`.
* `certificate` - For delivered orders, a URL to a delivery certificate for the order.
* `confirmed_at` - Time at which the order was confirmed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `delayed_at` - Time at which the order's expected_delivery_year was delayed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `delivered_at` - Time at which the order was delivered. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `delivery_details` - Details about the delivery of carbon removal for this order. See [`delivery_details`](#delivery_details) below.
* `expected_delivery_year` - The year this order is expected to be delivered. If the year is in the past, the order is a spot purchase and will be delivered within 30 days of purchase.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `product_substituted_at` - Time at which the order's product was substituted for a different product. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `status` - The current status of this order. Possible values: `awaiting_funds`, `canceled`, `confirmed`, `delivered`, `open`.

<a id="delivery_details"></a>
### `delivery_details`

The `delivery_details` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `delivered_at` - Time at which the delivery occurred. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `location` - Specific location of this delivery. See [`delivery_details.location`](#delivery_details.location) below.
* `metric_tons` - Quantity of carbon removal supplied by this delivery.
* `registry_url` - Once retired, a URL to the registry entry for the tons from this delivery.
* `supplier` - A supplier of carbon removal. See [`delivery_details.supplier`](#delivery_details.supplier) below.

<a id="delivery_details.location"></a>
### `delivery_details.location`

The `delivery_details.location` attribute supports:

* `city` - The city where the supplier is located.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country where the supplier is located.
* `latitude` - The geographic latitude where the supplier is located.
* `longitude` - The geographic longitude where the supplier is located.
* `region` - The state/county/province/region where the supplier is located.

<a id="delivery_details.supplier"></a>
### `delivery_details.supplier`

The `delivery_details.supplier` attribute supports:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `info_url` - Link to a webpage to learn more about the supplier.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `locations` - The locations in which this supplier operates. See [`delivery_details.supplier.locations`](#delivery_details.supplier.locations) below.
* `name` - Name of this carbon removal supplier.
* `object` - String representing the object’s type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `climate.supplier`.
* `removal_pathway` - The scientific pathway used for carbon removal. Possible values: `biomass_carbon_removal_and_storage`, `direct_air_capture`, `enhanced_weathering`, `marine_carbon_removal`.

<a id="delivery_details.supplier.locations"></a>
### `delivery_details.supplier.locations`

The `delivery_details.supplier.locations` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `city` - The city where the supplier is located.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country where the supplier is located.
* `latitude` - The geographic latitude where the supplier is located.
* `longitude` - The geographic longitude where the supplier is located.
* `region` - The state/county/province/region where the supplier is located.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a climate order using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_climate_order.offset
  id = "climorder_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_climate_order.offset
  identity = {
    id = "climorder_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the climate order.

Using `terraform import`, import a climate order using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_climate_order.offset climorder_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `amount`, so an imported order has none in state. Importing an order that was bought by `amount` and configuring `amount` plans a replacement.
